cause: No repository CI; the documented browser command uses an occupied evidence directory.
event: An agent skips browser checks or cannot attach a fresh review result.
consequence: A UI regression may be proposed for acceptance without repeatable evidence.
evidence: repository-safeguards.json shows no tracked CI; browser-original-command.txt exits 1 before launch; output-only adapter passes 18/18.
reason: Skipping manual checks is possible. The exact fresh-run barrier is reproduced. Impact is moderate because wrong feedback affects a fictional demo, without real bookings.
mitigation: Proposal 01: add limited-permission CI, a fresh output-directory option and the documented rerun command.
verification: Apply only after approval; exercise new output path and overwrite guard, run all existing checks and inspect workflow. Cloud execution requires a later authorized push.
residualReason: New output path produced 18/18 browser checks; both overwrite guards passed; CI file/commands/shell structure verified locally. Likelihood falls to unlikely; impact is unchanged. First hosted CI execution and required-check enforcement remain unverified.

cause: AGENTS.md has no explicit worktree/port isolation, credential boundary or approval gate before merge and acceptance.
event: An asynchronous agent shares state or treats passing tests as permission to accept changes.
consequence: User work or the review boundary could be compromised.
component: AGENTS.md Engineering rules and Verification commands
evidence: AGENTS.before.md preserves the full original document; task 06 review maps each required boundary.
reason: The safeguards are absent, but no unauthorized action is observed. Moderate impact is appropriate for this small repository and preserved Git history.
mitigation: Proposal 02: add concise isolation, no-secret, evidence and explicit human-review rules.
verification: Inspect exact AGENTS diff, confirm all AC rules and five-room scope remain, then record human approval and full regression results.
residualReason: Approved rules now require isolated tasks, no credentials, evidence and human review. The actual approval gate was used. Likelihood falls to unlikely; impact remains moderate. Written rules are not technical access enforcement.

cause: Locked dependencies include affected Vite 5.4.8, Vitest 2.1.9 and an unused Supabase path to ws 8.18.3.
event: Vulnerable tooling is used with an untrusted origin or privileged test-server exposure; an unused dependency may later become active.
consequence: Development source or privileged tooling may be accessed outside the intended origin.
evidence: npm-audit.json: 25 affected packages, two critical; production-only audit: one high package. installed-dependencies.json and ws-path.json confirm paths. vite-cors.json observes Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on fictional source. Vendor advisories cited in security-assessment.md.
reason: Affected versions and permissive HTTP behavior are observed. No exploit is attempted; UI/API server conditions are not used by npm test. Supabase is not imported by app source. These checks do not establish a vulnerability in the static published bundle.
mitigation: Owner must plan a compatible toolchain/dependency update and rerun regressions. Until then use trusted dedicated project browser sessions, no privileged test API/UI, no credentials and no network-exposed dev server. Loopback alone does not fix the Vite advisory.
verification: After a separately reviewed update: fresh npm ci/audit, inspect affected paths and server behavior, run full/browser/build checks.
residualReason: No dependency version changed. Full audit still reports 25 affected packages. Existing trusted-use/no-privileged-server controls have an owner; a reviewed compatible upgrade is outstanding. Score stays 4.

event: A contributor adds a new test without updating the include list.
consequence: The test is silently absent from the default suite.
evidence: test-discovery.txt: an existing temporary diagnostic test is excluded and exits 1 with No test files found; the file was then removed from the isolated worktree.
reason: The omission is reproduced. Current 81 tests still run; impact is minor for the present fixed suite and review can require explicit collection.
mitigation: Proposal 02 documents collection checks; later consider a reviewed glob while excluding controlled historical test copies.
verification: Check runner collection for every new test; retain current 81-test coverage.
residualReason: The include allowlist is unchanged. The playbook now requires proof of test collection; the underlying omission risk remains scored 2.

cause: README describes a sibling Practice07 artifact directory and old publication status that do not match the current checked-out context.
event: An agent follows historical paths/status as current instructions.
consequence: Review time is wasted or the wrong evidence is selected.
component: README.md Assignment artifacts and final Practice09 paragraph
evidence: documentation-inventory.json records absent sibling and the live URL check; original README is preserved in the Git baseline.
reason: The stale context exists. Core run commands work, and no behavior failure is observed, so impact stays minor.
mitigation: Keep audit/source references explicit; revise historical guidance in a separately reviewed documentation update.
verification: Resolve links and compare stated evidence with the current tree.
residualReason: Historical README content remains outside the approved patch scope. Practice10 references and evidence are explicit, but no general documentation cleanup is claimed.

cause: The helper checks the reference clock for finiteness but not its day range.
event: A future direct caller supplies currentMinutes=-1.
consequence: The helper accepts a request against a nonsensical reference clock.
evidence: source-probes.txt records valid=true with -1. CurrentTimeControl clamps normal UI input; no external caller or failing user scenario was found.
reason: The helper edge is observed, but acceptance for out-of-domain callers is unspecified and the normal UI does not supply it. This is not established as an AC violation.
mitigation: Clarify the public helper clock domain before any behavior change.
verification: Agree the reference-clock contract and add a regression only if required.
residualReason: No external caller contract was added. UI still supplies its clamped clock; this remains a plausible/unverified helper-domain concern.

cause: Hypothesis: endpoint overlap or fixture mutation is wrong.
event: Availability rejects a touching request or changes caller data.
consequence: AC4 or AC5 would be violated.
evidence: 81/81 tests include both endpoints, real overlap and frozen data; 18/18 browser checks and source-probes.txt agree. Source filters by room and sorts a copy.
reason: Score is for the hypothetical consequence only. No present defect is found; it is not an actionable confirmed risk.
mitigation: Keep the existing regression assertions; no behavior patch justified.
verification: Preserve AC4/AC5 coverage in each accepted change.
residualReason: Existing source/tests/browser evidence continue to contradict the proposed defect. Score describes hypothetical impact, not a confirmed bug.

cause: Hypothesis: fixture display inserts raw HTML or tracked source exposes credentials.
event: An input is interpreted as script or a credential is published.
component: BookingPanel React text rendering; src/; tracked text/configuration
evidence: source-probes.txt confirms synthetic script text is escaped; repository-safeguards.json has no raw HTML sinks and no matches in the limited 304-file credential-pattern scan.
reason: No supporting path or credential is found. The sample scan is not a full secret audit and does not certify all files/history.
mitigation: Keep fictional fixtures and no-secret boundaries; no invented XSS fix.
verification: Review new HTML sinks/credentials and do not expose actual secret values.
residualReason: The escaped-render and bounded pattern scan are unchanged. Score describes a hypothetical scenario, not a demonstrated vulnerability.
